method: Maat concolic/symbolic emulation of the -O0 -static -no-pie binaries. No separate taint bit: attacker input is made concolic (symbolic var + concrete valuation) and 'tainted' == the value's symbolic expression still depends on an input variable. CT: function-level emulation of pow_branch/pow_ct (RIP := entry, SysV args, sentinel return) to bypass static-glibc startup; only the exponent (rsi, stdin value 5) is a concolic var, and a conditional branch leaks iff its Constraint.contained_vars() include 'exp'. DNS: the flag byte is built bit-by-bit (Concat of Var(1)/Cst(1)) so single bits can be tainted; output dependence is tested by dual concretization.

ct.initial_taint: exponent only: rsi low-32 `e` (stdin secret, value 5) is a concolic Var(32) 'exp'; base=rdi=7 and mod=rdx=101 concrete public constants (RSA/DH threat model).
ct.detection_rule: For each conditional BRANCH event, leak iff the secret var 'exp' is in engine.info.branch.cond.contained_vars().
ct.verdict: vuln = TRUE POSITIVE (1 tainted conditional-branch site, executed 32x, cond depends on the secret exponent var 'exp'); ct = TRUE NEGATIVE (0 tainted branches). No false positive, no false negative -- matches microtaint (vuln>=1, ct=0).

dns.workload: test_bitpacked_dns.c LDNS_OPCODE_WIRE: AND AL,0x78 (24 78) then SHR AL,3 (C0 E8 03)
dns.verdict: Maat is bit-granular symbolic: an 8-bit value is a Concat of eight independent 1-bit terms, so a SINGLE flag bit can be made symbolic in isolation. Tainting only QR(bit7): AL output is CLEAN (AND 0x78 masks bit7 away, dual-concretization shows no dependence). Tainting only OPCODE(bits6..3): AL output is TAINTED (bits survive AND+SHR into the low nibble). Maat therefore DISCRIMINATES QR from OPCODE -- the bit-granularity discriminator the byte engines (Triton/libdft/Taintgrind) fail: they can only taint the whole AL byte and conflate the two.

notes: All numbers produced by real Maat emulation via .venv_maat/bin/python (drivers: detect_maat_ct.py, detect_maat_dns.py; raw traces: results/_maat_ct_raw.json, results/_maat_dns_raw.json). Full-process emulation of the static -no-pie binaries is blocked by unemulated glibc-startup syscalls, so the CT target functions are driven directly at their entry points -- the sanctioned function-level fallback. CT: Maat resolves the branch condition symbolically and matches microtaint exactly (vuln = 1 leak site at 0x402fa8 executed 32x, ct = 0). DNS: unlike the byte-granular engines, Maat expresses per-bit taint (Concat of 1-bit terms) and correctly reports QR(bit7)->output CLEAN vs OPCODE(bits6..3)->output TAINTED, i.e. it CAN discriminate benign QR from security-relevant OPCODE. Bit-granularity is the discriminator.
